name: North Carolina

laws.cite: 28 CFR Part 35, Subpart H (ADA Title II web & mobile rule, 2024; dates extended by IFR 2026-07663)
laws.summary: Federal floor: state and local government web content and mobile apps must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA; the April 2026 IFR moved compliance to 2027-04-26 (pop. 50,000+) and 2028-04-26 (smaller entities and special districts).

policy_docs.title: State of North Carolina Digital Accessibility and Usability Standard v1.1 (2025-01-16)

applies_to: All state agency public-facing websites and digital services, incl. those run by contractors; internal sites encouraged.

deadlines.what: ADA Title II rule: state government and local governments with population 50,000+ must conform web content and mobile apps to WCAG 2.1 AA (extended from 2026-04-24 by DOJ IFR effective 2026-04-20)
ADA Title II rule: local governments under 50,000 and special district governments (extended from 2027-04-26)

requires: All agency websites and digital services adhere to WCAG 2.1 AA
Agency Digital Accessibility Coordinator requested by NCDIT (engages vendors, reviews ACR/VPATs)
Mobile-first responsive design; required links; mobile app privacy policy
mobile: explicit — standard covers public websites and apps, with a mobile-first design section and mobile application requirements.
procurement: Coordinators review/request ACRs/VPATs from vendors (NCDIT guidance); no mandatory clause verified.
enforcement: No penalty; NCDIT warns agencies without a coordinator face higher ADA Title II legal risk.
notes: Standard cites N.C.G.S. 143B-1320(a)(17), 143B-1376 and 75-61(10) as related statutes; these are general IT/definitions provisions and were not opened. No NC accessibility-specific statute found. Coordinator appointment is a request, not a codified mandate.
